name: DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B

lineage.how_derived: converted to block-diffusion text generation on the Gemma 4 MoE foundation

purpose: Open-weights model that generates text with discrete diffusion instead of token-by-token autoregression, to raise generation speed (tokens per second) at small batch sizes on a single accelerator while keeping a MoE footprint suitable for local execution (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card links the Gemma 4 license page, which is plain Apache License 2.0 (gemma.ai/resources/apache-2/, Google DeepMind, summarizer read); same as the Gemma 4 records.

architecture.attention: sliding window 1024 with a full-attention layer every 6th layer; bidirectional attention over a 256-token canvas
architecture.why_this_design: Card: 'engineered to reduce the sequential bottlenecks of standard causal language models'. The encoder prefills the prompt and caches the KV; the decoder denoises a 256-token canvas in parallel (15-20 tokens per forward pass), the finished canvas is re-encoded and appended, then the next canvas follows; simpler prompts and code need fewer denoising steps. Built on the 26B A4B MoE with 8 of 128 experts active for a low memory footprint.

variants.notes: 598,561 downloads, created 2026-06-09; community GGUF builds not checked

pc-12gb.notes: same weight footprint as Gemma 4 26B A4B

pc-16gb.notes: weights as the AR sibling; the diffusion sampler is compute-heavy per step

engine_support.notes: Needs a diffusion sampling loop (canvas denoising, encoder re-pass); autoregressive engines cannot run it unchanged. Support in llama.cpp not checked.

benchmarks.name: Generation speed, low batch, H100 FP8

strengths: 15-20 tokens per forward pass: a diffusion LM at Gemma 4 26B-A4B-adjacent quality (5-20 points lower on vendor tables)
Adaptive compute: structured tasks such as code need fewer denoising steps
Same Apache-2.0 license and weight size as the AR sibling
weaknesses: Quality is below Gemma 4 26B A4B on every vendor benchmark (AIME 2026 69.1 vs 88.3, LiveCodeBench 69.1 vs 77.1, Tau2 56.2 vs 68.2, MRCR 128K 32.0 vs 44.1)
No speed number for consumer GPUs

user_reports.summary: Field report: running DiffusionGemma 26B as the model behind a full Claude Code style agent on a single RTX 5090 under WSL2 (what worked and what did not); thread body not read.

soft.maturity: Google DeepMind, 598K downloads; several chat-template fixes merged by the community.

tona_fit.reason: Interesting for the decode-bound consumer-GPU case (parallel 256-token canvases trade compute for fewer weight reads), Apache-2.0 (text read), but the vendor numbers show a 5-20 point quality loss against its own autoregressive sibling and no consumer-GPU speed is published. Worth a speed measurement once an engine can run the sampler; not an offer on quality.
blockers: quality below Gemma 4 26B A4B on all vendor benchmarks

open_questions: Decode speed on a consumer GPU (RTX 5090 field report body unread)
llama.cpp or other engine support for the diffusion sampler
Independent quality results (a community eval PR exists, not read)
